title: Normality and properness of an existing finite geometric quotient
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a normal proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let a finite group $H$ act on $X$ over $k$. Here normal means that each local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Suppose a $k$-scheme $Z$ and an $H$-invariant morphism of $k$-schemes $q:X\to Z$ (compatible with the structure morphisms to $\operatorname{Spec}k$) are already given such that $q$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism], its geometric fibres are $H$-orbits, and $\mathcal O_Z=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^H$ (sections are precisely the invariant sections). Suppose also that every invariant morphism of $k$-schemes from $X$ to a $k$-scheme factors uniquely through $q$ by a morphism of $k$-schemes. Then $Z$ is normal and proper of finite type over $k$, and is Noetherian (it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]). Neither the existence of a quotient nor an ample sheaf or projective embedding on $Z$ is asserted. The group action may be nonfaithful and $X$ may be empty or disconnected.

source.place: Agent-formulated general prerequisite for the existing quotients in Expose X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.151. Algebraic finite-type input: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00IS (Artin--Tate); properness inputs: morphisms.tex Tags 09MQ(4) (separated target of a finite surjection) and 03GN (universally closed image). Normality follows by invariant subrings of the normal domain factors on a finite affine inverse image. This statement does not assert projective quotient existence or projectivity.
